bib.title: EfficientNet: Rethinking Model Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks

question: Is there a principled method to scale up ConvNets that achieves better accuracy and efficiency than scaling depth, width or resolution alone?
hypothesis: Balancing network width, depth and resolution by scaling each with a constant ratio gives better accuracy and efficiency than scaling a single dimension.
contributions: Empirical study showing depth, width and resolution must be balanced when scaling ConvNets
Compound scaling method with one coefficient phi
EfficientNet family (B0-B7): NAS-found B0 baseline scaled by compound scaling, state-of-the-art ImageNet accuracy with far fewer parameters and FLOPS, and strong transfer results

method.summary: Scale depth d=alpha^phi, width w=beta^phi, resolution r=gamma^phi with alpha*beta^2*gamma^2 ~ 2, constants chosen by a small grid search at phi=1 on the small baseline. A multi-objective NAS (accuracy and FLOPS) gives EfficientNet-B0, scaled to B1-B7 and also applied to MobileNets and ResNet-50.
method.task: ImageNet image classification and transfer to 8 image datasets

datasets.name: ImageNet (ILSVRC)
datasets.split: 25K random training images held out as minival for early stopping; final accuracy on the original validation set; test set (100k images) also submitted

models.name: EfficientNet-B0
models.architecture: MBConv (mobile inverted bottleneck) with squeeze-and-excitation, found by multi-objective NAS in the MnasNet search space; 9 stages (Table 1); FLOPS target 400M

models.name: MobileNetV1, MobileNetV2, ResNet-50
models.architecture: scaled by depth, width, resolution or compound

models.name: GPipe, ResNet-152, ResNeXt-101, SENet, NASNet-A, AmoebaNet and others

training.regularisation: stochastic depth with survival probability 0.8; AutoAugment; SiLU (Swish-1) activation; batch norm momentum 0.99

other.early stopping: on 25K-image minival; early-stopped checkpoint evaluated on the ImageNet validation set
other.transfer: borrows training settings from Kornblith et al. 2019 and Huang et al. 2018: ImageNet-pretrained checkpoints finetuned on new datasets (hyperparameters not given)

inference.samples: Latency: average over 20 runs; ImageNet accuracy single-crop, single-model

parameters.latency: batch size 1, single core of Intel Xeon CPU E5-2690

eval.protocol: Single runs as far as stated; no seeds, variance or significance test reported. Single-crop single-model; ensembles, multi-crop and Instagram-pretrained models omitted.

limits: Training hyperparameters for transfer finetuning, batch size, epochs, hardware and compute are not given in this paper.
alpha, beta, gamma come from a grid search on B0 only; the authors concede better values might come from searching near a large model but this is too costly.
Compound scaling gains depend on the baseline; the authors say scaling effectiveness depends heavily on the baseline network, so they ran NAS for B0.
SOTA gains mix architecture, scaling and training settings (AutoAugment, SiLU, stochastic depth); the paper says gains come from all three.
FLOPS-based (not latency-based) search; latency measured on one CPU only, no GPU/TPU latency.
No seeds or variance. Single-model single-crop numbers; ImageNet SOTA claim dated (2019).
The claim that FLOPS scale as d, w^2, r^2 assumes convolutions dominate.
